questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to move.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
To the left until backing is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to move.
questions.explanation: When backing a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: At what air pressure will an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?
questions.correctAnswerText: Between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: An automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: What happens when an air supply control is in the "emergency" position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes apply.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is set to "emergency," the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes apply.

questions.question: Compared to empty rigs, fully-loaded rigs are:

options.text: Just as likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity due to cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Changing lanes quickly in a combination vehicle can cause:

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that results in a rollover.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that results in a rollover.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect caused by rearward amplification can result in a rollover if you change lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle.

questions.question: What causes more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths?
questions.correctAnswerText: Rollovers.
questions.explanation: More than half of truck driver deaths in accidents are caused by rollovers. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low to the ground and centered on your rig. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: How should you apply brakes on a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The same way as a vehicle without ABS.
While putting the vehicle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way as a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: You should brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: How does watching the road ahead help you drive safely?

options.text: It is more dangerous than only watching your mirrors.
It does not help you drive more safely.
It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you avoid sudden lane changes.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous in combination vehicles. Looking ahead for obstacles lets you plan ahead and avoid needing to make sudden lane changes.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.correctAnswerText: A triple combination.
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most at risk for rollovers from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn over trailers.
questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect can cause a trailer to turn over during a lane change. To avoid this, make lane changes slowly and safely.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible in the trailer.
Placed as low as possible in the trailer.
Placed on the passenger side of the trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible in the trailer.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight low to the ground to prevent rollovers. Do not place weight on one side of the trailer, as this can cause leaning and increase rollover risk.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Usually have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer, heavier, and more prone to rollover. They need more skill to drive safely.

questions.question: To prevent a rollover, a driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep cargo low.
questions.explanation: Load cargo as close to the ground as possible. This keeps the vehicle's center of gravity low and helps prevent rollovers, especially during quick turns.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.correctAnswerText: Control line
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line. It carries air to the trailer brakes and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: Push in the trailer air supply control to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Send air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on downhill slopes.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when transporting cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. Air can leak out and the brakes will release. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes will activate.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If pressure is lost in this line, the emergency trailer brakes will activate automatically.

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Sends air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sends air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two purposes. It sends air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
Only the rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the ones on the rear trailer. This makes sure air reaches all brakes and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should:

options.text: Be used only to test the trailer brakes.
Be used together with the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving, as it could cause a skid. Never use it for parking because air pressure may leak out and release the brakes.
